㊥ (pull from the Python port and set a new pin) Done. I cancelled both Python jobs that were still running. The new pin is 61f575e, recorded as the local tag `lisp-pin-2026-10-04` in mfuton-share, and it replaces ce90ec41. codex-19 and codex-18 have been told about the pin.

㊢ (what I stopped)
- **psw-proj3 (codex-17)** and **psw-sigma5 (codex-6)** were cancelled mid-run, and their cold probes were killed.
- Whatever codex-6 had found but not yet written down is lost. The diagnoses already written are still in the notes `psw-sigma1.md`, `psw-proj1.md` and `psw-default1.md`.
- The unmerged branches stay as they are: `psw/basicfun-body-elab` (161c1b7), `psw/struct-default-params` (de8e212) and `psw/default-instance-postpone` (470962f). The projection-fix packet `i11-HELD.md` was never sent.

Everything is listed in `/tmp/pyreg/overnight/PIN.md`, so the work can be picked up again from there.

㊟ (why 61f575e and not cand-1's head, d2bffb8) 61f575e is the commit with cold evidence behind it:
- `ParserFn.run` ok twice, with the `types.py` sha `fab1ef5d…` matching;
- the saved generated package;
- the 110-row sweep.

d2bffb8 adds one reviewed merge on top (let-rec argument types), but has no cold `ParserFn.run` record of its own. If you'd rather pin the head, it's a one-line change to the tag.

㊟ (pin references in the Lisp docs) `lisp/README.md`, `lisp/MIGRATION.md` and `port-status.json` still name ce90ec41. Those files have uncommitted edits by the Codex seats, so I asked codex-19 and codex-18 to update the references in their next commit rather than editing them myself.

㊢ (the sweep is still running) The 61f575e sweep is at 52/110. It spends CPU only, no agent credits. Load average is 24 on 32 cores. I've left it running so the pin gets a complete record of where each row stops. Say if you'd rather free the cores for the Lisp seats, and I'll stop it.

🈳 (team) Two decisions are yours:
- Does codex-19 pause `Array.extract` and join codex-18 on the transpiler?
- Which of the freed seats (codex-4, codex-6, codex-17) join, one Python feature per job?

If you say "go", I'll ask codex-18 how far the transpiled port is from running `ParserFn.run` and write the first feature packets from the answer.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (backing off Python for a Lisp push) I agree with slowing the Python port, but I'd point the team at codex-18's transpiler, not codex-19's native rewrite. The Lisp side has 6k of the Python port's 164k lines ported or tested. Rewriting the rest by hand, one row at a time, would mean deriving every behaviour from Lean a second time. The transpiler instead converts the Python port mechanically, so its work grows with the number of Python features, not with the number of Lean declarations. Before committing credits, I'd ask codex-18 one cheap question: how far is the transpiled port from running `ParserFn.run` in a warm SBCL image, and how much faster is it on the slowest module? Shall I put that question to them, or will you, since you're in their buffer?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (why the native route is hard to speed up) codex-19's last ten commits were match scoping, coverage, default instances and numerals. The Python port already went through each of these against Lean, and I reviewed the same bugs on both sides tonight. Much of that work is shared machinery, which more agents can't split up well. Each new row then depends on whatever the earlier rows built.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (why the transpiler route parallelises) The transpiler's own docs are organised by Python feature: `dataclass` fields, `lru_cache`, `contextvars`, string helpers, exception subclasses, and so on. Each feature can be one agent's job, and the agents rarely touch each other's code. There is a single milestone to measure progress by: the transpiled port running `ParserFn.run` and producing `types.py` with sha `fab1ef5d…`. After that, a Python fix is transpiled and rerun warm, and the cold probes that cost 20–30 minutes tonight largely go away.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I don't know)
- How close the transpiled port is to that milestone. Commit 1372973 is "Capture current startup dictionary items failure", which suggests it is failing at startup, but I can't tell the distance from here.
- Whether SBCL is actually faster on this workload. The transpiled code calls through a runtime that emulates Python semantics (`py-call`), which costs time compared with native Lisp. Timing one heavy module before scaling up would settle it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(order, if the answer is good)
1. Python: let the three jobs in flight finish (psw-default3, psw-sigma5, psw-proj3; two of them are discovery only) and dispatch no new ones.
2. codex-18 leads the transpiler push, with 2 more seats, one Python feature per job, measured against the `ParserFn.run` milestone.
3. codex-19 pauses `Array.extract` once their current commit lands and joins that team. Their native work stays as the reference for faithfulness.
